title: Vesper and the Orchard
premise: In 1911, in the river town of Vesper, apprentice clockmaker Petra Zhou is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock just as the army requisitions the town and seizes the harbor ledger that records every family's citizenship papers. When evacuation berths are announced for a single ship, the Zhou family discovers their names were struck from the ledger years ago by a clerk's grudge — and the officer who can restore them wants Petra to sabotage the master clock so the requisition can be backdated. Petra must choose between restoring time (and their family's legal existence) or keeping the clock honest and finding justice outside the law. In the end, Petra repairs the clock but forges one page of the ledger, trading their own name away so their grandmother boards the last berth; the novel closes with Petra staying behind under a new name, keeper of the observatory, as history finally happens to them.
about_author: Z. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former horologist's assistant who spent a decade restoring municipal tower clocks across coastal towns before turning to fiction. They write historical novels about ordinary people caught in the machinery of empires.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Petra Zhou, POV: arrives at the observatory to repair the master clock, establishing their belief that history belongs to other people. Through meticulous gearwork scenes we meet Grandmother Wei, who keeps the family's papers sewn into her coat lining. Emotional beat: quiet pride and the comfort of routine before the world breaks it.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Petra, POV: soldiers occupy Vesper at dawn; an officer named Captain Aldous Rennick posts notices claiming the harbor ledger proves which families may remain. The Zhou name appears struck through with an old clerk's annotation. Emotional beat: disbelief curdling into fear as neighbors begin choosing sides.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Memory
chapters.summary: Grandmother Wei, POV: she reveals the strike-through dates to the year her husband testified against a customs clerk, Ivo Brandt, who now serves Rennick. She burns nothing and confesses everything. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited grievance and the first hint that the past was never elsewhere.

chapters.title: Terms of Repair
chapters.summary: Petra, POV: Rennick visits the observatory privately and offers restoration of the Zhou name in exchange for making the master clock run slow — enough to falsify the requisition's official timeline. Petra refuses too quickly, too politely. Emotional beat: shame at how easily they almost said yes.

chapters.title: Berths
chapters.summary: Multiple short POVs (Wei, neighbor Tomas Ilic, dockworker Sefa): the last ship is announced, four berths per registered family, none for the unregistered. The orchard by the observatory becomes a camp for the struck-through families. Emotional beat: communal grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Clock Keeps
chapters.summary: Petra, POV: inside the clock's case Petra finds decades of maintenance notes proving Brandt falsified ledgers long before the requisition — evidence no court will touch while the army holds the town. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, corrupting realization that paper makes truth, and Petra could make paper.

chapters.title: The Slow Hand
chapters.summary: Petra, POV: Petra begins secretly slowing the clock anyway — not for Rennick, but to buy the camp families hours during nightly document raids, timing them to darkness. Wei discovers it and, instead of condemning, teaches Petra forgery strokes learned in another country's upheaval. Emotional beat: complicity transformed into craft.

chapters.title: Brandt's Orchard
chapters.summary: Tomas Ilic, POV: Brandt leads a raid on the orchard camp; Sefa is taken, and the forged pages nearly surface. Petra watches justice fail through someone else's eyes. Emotional beat: rage and the collapse of the belief that cleverness alone can save anyone.

chapters.title: Eleven Fifty-Nine
chapters.summary: Petra, POV (climax): the night before departure, Petra restores the master clock to perfect time, then forges a single restored ledger page bearing one Zhou name — and strikes out their own. Confronted by Rennick at the top of the observatory, Petra lets the clock's chime expose his falsified timeline to the assembled officers below. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into certainty.

chapters.title: Vesper Time
chapters.summary: Petra, POV (resolution): Grandmother Wei boards the last berth; Petra remains under the name 'Vesper Zhou,' apprenticed openly to the observatory. Brandt is arrested by his own side; Rennick is quietly reassigned, unpunished — justice partial, survival complete. Petra winds the clock and, for the first time, feels history happening to them and chooses to keep it running. Emotional beat: bittersweet, resolute peace.
